body:
CVC informed Advent several weeks ago of its intention to exit the signed acquisition agreement after carrying out a forensic review of Irca’s finances.

CVC Capital Partners plans to withdraw from its nearly €3bn ($3.30bn) acquisition of Italian ingredients maker Irca from Advent International, opening the prospect of arbitration between the firms.

The Financial Times (FT), citing unnamed sources, reported that CVC informed Advent several weeks ago of its intention to exit the signed acquisition agreement after carrying out a forensic review of Irca’s finances.

The transaction had been due to close in the fourth quarter of this year.

Under the agreement, the matter would move to arbitration if the parties do not resolve the dispute.

“Extensive forensic analysis of the information that was provided to us during due diligence revealed that the transaction is no longer viable,” Luxembourg-based CVC said in a statement to the FT.

The firm added that it was “guided by its fiduciary duties” and that it was “in the best interests of our investors and wider stakeholders, to not proceed”.

Investment Monitor has contacted CVC for comment.

Advent rejected CVC’s proposed withdrawal and said it expected the buyer to complete the transaction.

“Advent strongly rejects CVC’s attempt to withdraw from a signed, binding agreement to acquire Irca. The transaction with CVC was agreed following extensive due diligence, and we stand behind the integrity of the sale process,” the firm said.

Advent bought Irca in 2022 and began a sale process earlier this year.

It received several binding offers, with CVC chosen partly for its ability to complete the deal quickly, according to sources.

CVC has said Irca’s performance declined after the agreement was signed, leading to its forensic analysis.

Advent believes the agreement does not include conditions, or enough evidence, permitting CVC to withdraw.

Irca makes ingredients and semi-finished products for the pastry, bakery, chocolate, and ice cream markets.

The company has faced higher cocoa and other commodity prices, as well as weaker demand.

Separately, CVC said CVC Capital Partners VIII had agreed to sell its approximately 50% stake in vehicle glass repair and replacement provider Cary Group to a consortium comprising Nordic Capital, Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan and CPP Investments.
